transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
British police have arrested five men near a military airbase that's been used by U.S.
bombers to strike Iran.
They're being held on suspicion of preparing an act of terrorism.
Tristan Wilkinson is a counselor for the Cotswold District, where RAF Fairford is located.
He says police have been on alert in the area.
"There was a specific threat about six weeks ago from the Iranians on this base.
At the time, there was an increased surveillance around the area.
This is an operational base.
It's no secret that we have American bombers here that are taking part in what's happening
in the Middle East at the moment."
Police say an investigation is ongoing.
Lawmakers are frustrated over the administration's refusal to send hundreds of millions of dollars
allocated by Congress out to its intended recipients.
The maneuver, called a pocket rescission, is illegal that's according to the nonpartisan
watchdog agency, the Government Accountability Office, and Pierre's Eric McDaniel has more.
"Congress has the power of the purse.
They get to decide where and how money is spent.
But for the second year in a row, the president is making some of those decisions himself.
He withheld $800 million from programs that touch immigrant services, racial and sexual
minority work, and climate change programs.
And appropriators on the Hill are upset.
Republican Susan Collins of Maine says this is the most recent attempt by the White House
to undermine Congress's constitutional powers.
Her Democratic counterpart, Patty Murray of Washington, called it theft, and the top Democrat
on the House Budget Committee, Brandon Boyle, says, "Donald Trump knows he can't get these
cuts through Congress, so he is illegally making them through the back door."
Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
"High winds, heavy rain and large waves continue to pound the eastern U.S. at the sours.
The season's first nor'easter continues to sit just off the coast.
The rains have caused flooding throughout the region, and at one point power was knocked
out to tens of thousands of homes.
The storm has also disrupted travel up and down the coast."
In Hawaii, meanwhile, Hurricane Nolo continues to move away from the island chain.
The storm has now become a major hurricane, with wind speeds topping 111 miles an hour.
But as Hawaii Public Radio's Bill Dorman reports, the increasing wind speeds are not causing
major damage.
"The storm's impacts are lingering.
Strong and gusty winds are whipping across several islands, especially Maui and Hawaii
Island.
That's knocked out power to several thousand people, and floodwaters have swept through
some areas.
Even so, the storm did not cause as much damage as feared.
Hurricane Nolo is expected to reach its peak intensity Monday, even further from Hawaii's
shores."
For NPR News, I'm Bill Dorman in Honolulu.
Asian shares were mixed in trading Monday.
Japan's Nikkei dropped slightly, while Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 2 percent.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose seven-tenths.
Brent crude prices rose 1.8 percent.
This is NPR News.
Swiss voters have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to strengthen that country's neutrality.
The measure was backed by the right-wing Swiss People's Party.
It would have prevented Switzerland from joining punitive measures against other countries,
unless they were imposed by the United Nations.
The 2019 superhero-epic Avengers Endgame was back on top of box office charts this weekend.
NPR's Bob Mondello calls this encore edition a lucrative marketing gimmick.
"Marvel will be opening Avengers Doomsday in three months, and what better way to promote
it than to bring back Endgame?"
"Avengers!
Assemble."
With four minutes of unseen footage to stoke excitement for the new installment, fans showed
up hoping to catch a glimpse of Robert Downey Jr., returning not as Iron Man, but as a supervillain.
"For me, I'm doomed."
This weekend's $86 million in ticket sales puts Endgame, the second biggest earner in
Hollywood history, within striking distance of Avatar, currently the biggest, and it edged
the total box office haul for the 38-film Marvel Cinematic Universe above $35 billion.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
This week's college football rankings are out.
The top three spots remain the same with Texas, Georgia, and Notre Dame.
Miami moved to number four, while Ohio State moved up two spots to number five.
Defending Champions Indiana dropped a spot to number six despite beating Northwestern
Saturday, followed by Alabama.
Florida jumped 13 spots to number eight after winning convincingly over Ole Miss, which
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
